# The registered core (generated by experiments/generate_registered_core.py — do not edit by hand)

Generated by `experiments/generate_registered_core.py` on 2026-10-27 at commit d629423-dirty from configs/registered_rules.json, docs/open_decisions.md, docs/preregistration.md; do not edit by hand.

Every registered rule of this project, 12 of them, with the value in force, the reason the configuration gives for it, the decisions and amendment items its text names and the code that holds it. This is the short way into the registration: it restates `configs/registered_rules.json` and resolves its references, and it adds nothing of its own, so where it is thin the configuration is thin. The references are the ones the rule's own text names, which can include an item the rule replaced rather than the one that set it: `membrane_potential_build` names item 13 because item 35 superseded it.

`configs/registered_rules.json` is the single place each value is written; `tests/test_registration_matches_the_code.py` asserts the code still holds it; `docs/amendment_history.md` says how each value got there from `Amends:` trailers; `docs/preregistration.md` carries the hypotheses and the analyses these rules serve. This page says only what is registered now and where to read why.

## What each rule means

### `floor_rule` = `none`

No magnitude floor. The decision rests on the paired interval on model minus best baseline; effect sizes are reported in standard errors of the available precision. Registered 15 October 2026 (the owner: "no floor. paired interval").

- Enforced at: `experiments/score_confirmatory.py` --floor-rule default
- Origin: Registered 15 October 2026, with no decision id or amendment item named in the rule's text, so the row or item behind it has to be found by hand
- Superseded values: `0.05 fixed`, `0.041 macro and 0.028 micro fixed`, `realised half-width plus 0.005`

### `alpha_one_sided` = `0.05`

The tested model is a candidate at one-sided 0.05: H1 first, then its second-stage family by Holm at the same level, so the smaller of H2 and P1 faces 0.025 and the larger faces 0.05. Holm over eight hypotheses was withdrawn on 8 October 2026. The level was halved to 0.025 while two models were tested, where the union bound over two uncorrected tests put the familywise chance of a lucky pass at 2 x 0.025 = 0.05. With tested_models holding one model from 22 October 2026 there is no across-model multiplicity left, the familywise level is this level itself, and the halving no longer buys anything, so it was returned to 0.05 (the owner, 22 October 2026: "Move it back to the .05 alpha please with just one model now"; decision 9.78). This is the more permissive of the two readings of the same registered familywise 0.05 and it was taken before any lockbox was drawn.

- Enforced at: `experiments/score_confirmatory.py` --alpha default
- Decisions: 9.78 (`docs/open_decisions.md`)
- Superseded values: `0.025, one-sided, per model while two models were tested`

### `tested_models` = `confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or`

One model: the noisy-OR configuration of the linear-response encoder. The sigmoid head was dropped on 15 October 2026 because only noisy-OR has modules that can be read as pathways; the message-passing encoder moved to robustness_models on 22 October 2026 (the owner: "Defer it to robustness. I don't want it constraining things because this is more about mechanistically identifiably predictive nosology"). The registered reason is that only the linear-response encoder has a closed-form steady state, so only there can the sensitivity of a label to a sign-disputed edge, and hence whether a disputed sign is identifiable at all, be read without a training run. With one tested model the familywise chance of a lucky pass is the level the model is tested at, which is why alpha_one_sided returned to 0.05 in the same session (decision 9.78): the registered familywise 0.05 is unchanged and is now carried by one test rather than split across two.

- Enforced at: `configs/head_choice.json` chosen values
- Decisions: 9.78 (`docs/open_decisions.md`)
- Superseded values: `confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or and confirmatory_v2_linear_response_noisy_or, each at one-sided 0.025`

### `robustness_models` = `confirmatory_v2_message_passing_noisy_or`

Read and reported with their intervals outside the tested family, spending no alpha, as the two permutation readings have since 8 October 2026. The message-passing encoder sits here from 22 October 2026 so a conclusion of the tested model can be checked against a second encoder of a different inductive bias without that check constraining the registered family. A robustness reading that disagrees is reported as a disagreement and cannot withdraw the tested model's result; the corroboration a second tested model would have given is therefore given up, which is the cost the owner accepted.

- Enforced at: `configs/head_choice.json` robustness values, scored by experiments/score_confirmatory.py --models
- Origin: since 8 October 2026, with no decision id or amendment item named in the rule's text, so the row or item behind it has to be found by hand

### `bootstrap_unit` = `group`

A cluster bootstrap over leakage groups rather than perturbations, so the dependence among perturbations sharing disease annotations or targets stays inside a resample.

- Enforced at: `experiments/score_confirmatory.py` --bootstrap-unit default
- Origin: not stated in the rule, with no decision id or amendment item named in the rule's text, so the row or item behind it has to be found by hand

A symptom enters the macro average with at least five positives and one negative among the labelled rows.

- Enforced at: `experiments/score_confirmatory.py`, symbol `MINIMUM_POSITIVES_TO_SCORE`
- Origin: not stated in the rule, with no decision id or amendment item named in the rule's text, so the row or item behind it has to be found by hand

### `normalisation` = `forward_cone`

Each edge is divided by the destination's in-degree summed over every relation, counting only the edges whose source the seed can reach, per seed; unsigned row sums over the edges that carry are one. Amendment item 28 as narrowed by decision 9.16.

- Enforced at: `experiments/run_main_model.py` --normalisation default
- Decisions: 9.16 (`docs/open_decisions.md`)
- Amendment items: 28 (`docs/preregistration.md`)

### `validation_fold_rule` = `seed % num_validation_folds`

The early-stopping validation fold rotates with the seed over round(1 / 0.15) = 7 grouped folds, so seeds 0 to 4 use folds 0 to 4 and folds 5 and 6 never serve as validation. The registration said "fold 0" until 15 October 2026, which described seed 0 alone.

- Enforced at: `experiments/run_main_model.py` the validation_fold assignment
- Origin: not stated in the rule, with no decision id or amendment item named in the rule's text, so the row or item behind it has to be found by hand

### `label_likelihood` = `positive_unlabelled`

Every pair the label selection keeps is counted once, at its code length under a positive-unlabelled likelihood (models/positive_unlabelled_likelihood.py): a labelled positive -log(b + (1 - b) pi f), an unlabelled pair -log(1 - b) - log(1 - pi f) and an evidenced negative -log(1 - a f), f the probability that the link is real. The labelling propensity pi at the median literature popularity is w + (1 - w) r(t, s) per perturbation type and symptom, w the registered negative weight 0.2 and r(t, s) the cell's labelled share on the fit rows, which keeps every cell's registered constant optimum and is above every share; one popularity slope is learned when a literature table is named. The false-report rate b is 0; the power a of a never-above-placebo negative is amendment item 3's n_effective / (n_effective + 214.39), 0.5 where the label states no arm sizes. Replaces the weighted cross-entropy of amendment item 3 (a silent pair at 0.2, an evidenced negative at its placebo weight, a positive at its evidence weight); decision 9.90.

- Enforced at: `experiments/run_main_model.py` --label-likelihood default
- Decisions: 9.90 (`docs/open_decisions.md`)
- Amendment items: 3 (`docs/preregistration.md`)
- Superseded values: `weighted: a positive at its evidence weight, an unlabelled pair at 0.2, a never-above-placebo negative at 0.5 or n_effective / (n_effective + 214.39) (amendment item 3)`

### `membrane_potential_build` = `computed_from_the_pools`

VM_c is computed from the six ion pools with the weights of the linearised parallel-conductance (Millman) equation, and the changes_membrane_potential edges from the charge-moving reactions are not made, so the divisor at VM_c is 1 and the law arrives whole. Amendment item 35, the owner's ruling of 26 October 2026 in decision 9.87; it replaces item 13's computed_beside_the_reactions, under which the law arrived at 1 / (1 + R) of itself.

- Enforced at: `scripts/rebuild_data_layer.sh` --membrane-potential, on both build_neuronal_graph_variant.py calls
- Decisions: 9.87 (`docs/open_decisions.md`)
- Amendment items: 13 (`docs/preregistration.md`), 35 (`docs/preregistration.md`)

**6 of 12 rules name no decision id and no amendment item in their own text**, so the question an examiner asks first — who decided this and when — is answered by a date rather than by a row that can be read:

- `floor_rule`: Registered 15 October 2026
- `robustness_models`: since 8 October 2026
- `bootstrap_unit`: no date either
- `num_bootstrap`: no date either
- `minimum_positives_to_score`: no date either
